items.keyReason: Nobody is singular, so knows agrees with it. Everyone, someone, and anybody are also singular; their choices use plural verb forms.
items.difficultyReason: The intervening prepositional phrases add a small distraction, but every choice uses the same familiar singular-indefinite-pronoun pattern.
items.rule: Singular indefinite pronouns take singular present-tense verbs, regardless of an intervening prepositional phrase.

pairwiseChoices.reason: Both are singular indefinite pronouns followed by a prepositional phrase and an incorrectly plural verb; changing the pronoun and verb does not change the reasoning.
The verbs differ in agreement: have fails with Everyone, while knows agrees with Nobody. The sentence templates remain very similar.

Are is plural with singular Someone; knows is singular with singular Nobody. The same template makes the contrast easy.
Both use a singular indefinite pronoun and an incorrectly plural verb after a prepositional phrase; the copula versus lexical verb is a surface variation.

items.keyReason: The singular head noun bundle agrees with rests. Directions and posters are plural and need explain and need; the singular key needs opens.
items.difficultyReason: A reader must identify the head of each subject phrase despite a nearby noun, but each sentence has a short, familiar subject and present-tense verb.
items.rule: A present-tense verb agrees with the head of its subject phrase, not a noun in an intervening prepositional phrase.

pairwiseChoices.reason: Plural directions incorrectly takes explains; singular bundle correctly takes rests. The contrast requires locating the head noun.

acrossItems.assessment: Both are four-choice, full-sentence 'find the one with correct present-tense agreement' items. In each, the reader locates the subject head, ignores the intervening prepositional phrase, and checks the verb. Q01 narrows the heads to singular indefinite pronouns; Q02 varies singular and plural noun heads. The second item adds some variation, but the shared solving routine and all-correct-sentence format remain conspicuous.
